newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian tax police say seized Norilsk metal freed.
newsitem.headline: Russian tax police say seized Norilsk metal freed.

text.p: Russian tax authorities, in a statement released on Tuesday, said they had released metals confiscated from the Norilsk Nickel plant.

A statement from the State Tax Inspectorate faxed to Reuters said that an unspecified amount of metals destined for export and other property had been released as part of an ongoing government inquiry into Norilsk finances.

Yuri Oleinikov and Sergei Vetchinin, spokesmen for RAO Norilsky Nikel, had said earlier on Tuesday that metals worth 625 billion roubles had been seized by the tax authorities but that other tonnages were being exported according to plan.
Oleinikov had said the seized metal amounted to half a cargo.

The State Tax Inspectorate statement said Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin had signed an order at the end of last month calling for a financial review of the troubled Norilsk Nickel flagship combine.
The statement also said that measures involving confiscation of metals destined for export would be limited as part of the review.
The review would be carried out by the Finance and Industry Ministries, the State Property Committee, the tax authorities, export and hard currency control entities and other organisations, it said.
Oleinikov said that Norilsk ships out metal, which eventually ends up in Rotterdam, about twice a month, and that the last shipment went at the weekend.
Supplies were also coming out of the Pechenga nickel plant, a Norilsk subsidiary in the northern Murmansk region, he said.
